name: Wild Man Dan Brewery
description: Barn brewery pouring award-winning micro batches and offering homebrew workshops with Dan and his mountain porch hospitality. Wild Man Dan Brewery is Virginia's tiniest production brewery, where Dan brews award-winning small batches in his barn and happily teaches visitors the art of ale making while they sample Chai-Laxin or Dark Matter IPA.
image1Desc: Brick house with white porch, surrounded by trees and blooming flowers.

name: Wood Ridge Farm Brewery
description: Nestled in the heart of Lovingston, Wood Ridge Farm Brewery is an estate brewery that embodies the essence of 'dirt-to-glass' brewing. With a commitment to sustainability, we grow and malt our own grains on-site, allowing visitors to savor distinctive local beers while enjoying breathtaking views of the surrounding countryside. In addition to our craft brews, Lovingston itself offers a rich tapestry of history, featuring the Lovingston Historic District and its courthouse, both proudly listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Join us for a unique tasting experience where every sip tells a story of the land.
image1Desc: Wooden 'LOVE' sign with sunset backdrop, couple walking towards a garden.
amenities: Farm; Scenic Views; Seasonal Menu; Beer; Cider; Tastings

name: Devils Backbone Distilling Co.
description: Nestled within the scenic Devils Backbone Basecamp, Devils Backbone Distilling Co. invites visitors to savor the art of craft distilling in a relaxed and inviting atmosphere. Here, you can indulge in expertly crafted small-batch gin, rum, and brandy cocktails, all while enjoying the stunning views from the lounge and covered patio. Whether you’re a spirits enthusiast or simply looking to unwind, this distillery offers a unique experience that showcases local flavors and craftsmanship, making it a must-visit destination for those exploring the area. Come for the drinks, stay for the ambiance, and discover what makes Devils Backbone truly special!
image1Desc: People relax outdoors on wooden chairs under sunny skies, surrounded by trees.
amenities: Spirits; Cocktails; Outdoor Seating; Tastings; Beer

name: Silverback Distillery
description: Nestled in the picturesque Blue Ridge Mountains, Silverback Distillery is a unique mother-daughter enterprise that brings a personal touch to craft distilling. Known as the nation’s only mother-daughter distilling duo, they create award-winning spirits, including gin, rye, bourbon, and a delightful honey liqueur, all sourced from local grains and pure mountain water. Visitors can savor a variety of tasting flights and indulge in innovative barrel-smoked cocktails at their charming Roseland stillhouse. Whether you’re a spirits connoisseur or a casual enthusiast, Silverback offers an engaging experience that celebrates the art of distillation in a stunning natural setting.
image1Desc: Blue building with lit windows, dusk sky, parking lot, and surrounding trees.
amenities: Spirits; Cocktails; Tastings; Scenic Views; Water Sports

name: Virginia Distillery Co.
description: Virginia Distillery Co. is a hidden gem nestled in the picturesque Blue Ridge Mountains, where visitors can experience the art of whiskey-making in a stunning setting. This 30-acre distillery, originally donated by Mr. W. B. D. Waller, offers guided tours that delve into the distillation process, showcasing their commitment to craftsmanship and local ingredients. Guests can enjoy tastings of their award-winning spirits, explore the scenic grounds, and even pair their whiskey with delicious offerings from the nearby Blue Mountain Brewery, making it a perfect destination for both connoisseurs and casual visitors alike.
image1Desc: Stone gate entrance to a large white house, surrounded by trees and hills.
amenities: Spirits; Museum; Tastings

name: Montebello Fish Hatchery
description: Discover the enchanting Montebello Fish Hatchery, nestled near the breathtaking Crabtree Falls. This educational haven offers guided tours that delve into the fascinating world of fish rearing, perfect for families and nature lovers alike. Stroll along the scenic nature trail, where vibrant pollinator plots attract a variety of butterflies and bees, enhancing your outdoor experience. After your visit, explore nearby attractions like Veritas Vineyards & Winery and Blue Mountain Brewery, making Montebello the perfect stop for a day of adventure and relaxation in Virginia’s stunning mountain landscape.
image1Desc: Sign for Montebello State Fish Hatchery amidst autumn trees by winding road.
amenities: Hiking; Biking; Fishing

name: One Forest
description: Nestled in the heart of Nellysford, One Forest is an innovative forest-based education and wellness space designed to immerse visitors in the beauty of nature. This unique destination emphasizes nature play and outdoor learning, offering enriching experiences for families and individuals alike. As you explore the surrounding area, don't miss nearby attractions like Inglewood Farm, Veritas Vineyards & Winery, and Blue Mountain Brewery, which add to the charm of this picturesque region. One Forest is currently in development, promising to be a haven for those seeking connection with nature and a deeper understanding of the environment. Whether you're looking to unwind in a serene setting or engage in hands-on learning, One Forest will soon be a must-visit spot for outdoor enthusiasts.
image1Desc: Tall white flowering plant in garden with wooden house and trees behind.
amenities: Outdoor Seating

name: Oak Ridge Estate
description: Nestled within a sprawling 5,000-acre plantation, Oak Ridge Estate is a captivating historical mansion that dates back to 1802. Acquired in the early 20th century by the influential Thomas Fortune Ryan, one of America's wealthiest men, the estate boasts stunning renovations including a formal Italian garden, a charming rotunda greenhouse, and a quaint railroad station. Visitors can explore the beautifully landscaped grounds while enjoying nearby attractions like the Montebello Fish Hatchery and Veritas Vineyards & Winery, making it a perfect destination for history enthusiasts and nature lovers alike. Experience the elegance of a bygone era and the serene beauty of Virginia’s countryside at Oak Ridge Estate.
image1Desc: Large white mansion with columns, surrounded by green lawn and trimmed shrubs.
amenities: Events

name: Swannanoa
description: Experience the elegance of Swannanoa, a stunning marble villa built in 1911, perched atop Afton Mountain. Open on select weekends for public tours, this architectural gem invites visitors to explore its exquisite Italianate design and beautifully landscaped gardens. Immerse yourself in the rich history and serene surroundings that make Swannanoa a captivating destination for architecture enthusiasts and nature lovers alike.
image1Desc: Vintage black car parked outside a large white mansion.
amenities: Outdoor Seating; Scenic Views; Tours

name: Blue Ridge Fruit Loop
description: Explore the Blue Ridge Fruit Loop, featuring 11 orchards and farms in Nelson and Amherst counties. From May to December, pick your own fruit while enjoying stunning views of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Visit highlights such as Inglewood Farm, Deer Creek Farm, and Montebello Fish Hatchery. Savor fine wines at Veritas Vineyards & Winery or Mountain and Vine Winery, and enjoy a craft brew from Blue Mountain Brewery. Don’t forget to stop by Basic Necessities for local treats. Experience a memorable day of exploration and flavor!
image1Desc: Clusters of ripe blackberries on bush, hand reaching in sunlight.

name: Glass Hollow Studio & Gallery
description: Nestled in the scenic Rockfish Valley, Glass Hollow Studio & Gallery invites you to explore the captivating world of glass art. Experience live glassblowing demonstrations and discover exquisite handcrafted pieces that showcase the beauty of this unique medium. Join us every Saturday in September for our popular 'Make Your Own Glass Pumpkin' workshops, where you can create a personal masterpiece to take home. Whether you're an art enthusiast or a curious beginner, there's something for everyone at our vibrant studio.

amenities: Museum; Retail

name: Blue Ridge Parkway Loops
description: Embark on an unforgettable cycling adventure along the stunning Blue Ridge Parkway, where you can choose between scenic 22- or 40-mile loops starting near Love, Virginia. As you pedal through this picturesque landscape, be captivated by breathtaking overlooks of the Shenandoah Valley and the thrill of Parkway climbs that challenge and reward with panoramic views. Don’t miss the chance to explore the Lower Shamokin Falls Trail, a hidden gem that offers a refreshing nature break. After your ride, unwind at the nearby Blue Mountain Brewery, where you can savor local brews and delicious fare. This cycling experience combines natural beauty, physical challenge, and a taste of local culture, making it a must-do for outdoor enthusiasts.
image1Desc: Sun setting over mountains with road and railing in foreground.
address: Milepost 16, Blue Ridge Parkway, Love, VA 22952
amenities: Biking; Hiking; Scenic Views

name: Oak Ridge Loop
description: The 29-mile Oak Ridge Loop offers a scenic cycling experience through Route 56 and Rockfish Valley backroads. Riders enjoy low-traffic farm lanes, historic estate views, and stretches along Route 29, featuring rolling hills before returning to the Oak Ridge parking area.
image1Desc: Stone cottage with green roof surrounded by trees and iron fence.
image2Desc: Old wooden mill with waterwheel by pond, surrounded by lush green trees.

accordionPanel2Content: The loop is considered moderate in length and moderate in difficulty, with gradual climbs, uneven footing, and natural trail surfaces.
accordionPanel3Content: Trail conditions may vary after storms or seasonal weather. Visitors should remain on the marked route to avoid erosion and confusion at intersections.

name: Woodson's Mill Loop
description: Embark on a scenic 24-mile biking adventure along the Woodson's Mill Loop, where history and nature intertwine. Starting at the charming historic gristmill in Lowesville, this route takes you through the picturesque countryside surrounding Massies Mill and along Route 680. Cyclists will be treated to stunning views of rolling hills, lush landscapes, and the tranquil sounds of the nearby Lower Shamokin Falls. After your ride, consider stopping by the Blue Mountain Brewery for a refreshing local brew, making this outing not just a ride, but a delightful experience that showcases the beauty and charm of the region.
image1Desc: Old wooden watermill surrounded by lush greenery, near a tranquil pond.
amenities: Biking; Scenic Views; Farm; Water Sports

name: Walton's Mountain Museum Loop
description: Embark on a scenic 31-mile biking adventure along the Walton's Mountain Museum Loop, where the charm of Schuyler's countryside unfolds before you. This picturesque route takes you past the serene James River and the lush Esmont farms, offering cyclists a chance to immerse themselves in the tranquil beauty of quiet ridge lines. As you pedal, be sure to soak in the natural splendor and, if time allows, consider stopping by the nearby Blue Mountain Brewery for a refreshing break. Whether you're a seasoned cyclist or a leisurely explorer, this loop promises a delightful blend of history, nature, and local culture.
image1Desc: Red brick building with American flag, labeled Schuyler Elementary School.
accordionPanel1Content: The Walton’s Mountain Museum Loop is a short walking route that connects outdoor paths with the historic Walton’s Mountain Museum. It provides an easy way to combine light outdoor activity with a visit to the museum.
accordionPanel2Content: The loop is short and considered easy, with gentle terrain suitable for most visitors. The path passes through open areas and light woodland near the museum grounds.
accordionPanel3Content: This loop works well as a casual walk before or after visiting the museum and does not require special preparation.
amenities: Biking; Hiking; Scenic Views; Museum; Farm; Water Sports

name: Virginia Blue Ridge Railway Trail
description: Explore the scenic 7-mile Virginia Blue Ridge Railway Trail, a crushed-stone path that winds gracefully alongside the Piney and Tye rivers. With dual trailheads, this versatile route is ideal for biking, walking, and horseback riding, catering to all outdoor enthusiasts. As you journey through the trail, delight in seasonal wildflower displays that enhance the serene landscape, providing a perfect backdrop for both leisurely rides and invigorating outings. Experience the beauty of nature and enjoy an unforgettable adventure in this stunning setting.
image1Desc: Trailhead sign and small building surrounded by trees under clear blue sky.
address: 3124 Patrick Henry Highway, Piney River, VA 22964
amenities: Biking; Equestrian; Scenic Views; Hiking; Water Sports

name: Nelson Scenic Loop
description: Discover the breathtaking 50-mile Nelson Scenic Loop, a perfect biking adventure that weaves through Routes 151 and 664, alongside the iconic Blue Ridge Parkway. Experience stunning mountain vistas, charming orchards, and delightful craft beverage stops as you traverse this scenic route. Enjoy picturesque waterfalls and sweeping views from the Piedmont foothills to the ridge-top summits, making every turn a new adventure. Embrace the beauty of nature and the thrill of exploration on this unforgettable journey.
image1Desc: Black butterfly on pale purple flowers with green leaves.
accordionPanel1Content:
The Nelson Scenic Loop is a self-guided driving route that showcases the landscapes, rural communities, and mountain views of Nelson County.

The loop is designed for leisurely exploration rather than point-to-point travel.
accordionPanel2Content:
The full route spans several dozen miles and travels through valleys, along ridgelines, and near rivers.

Road conditions range from gentle rural roads to winding mountain sections.
accordionPanel3Content:
The scenic loop can be driven in sections or completed in one outing. Drivers should allow time for pull-offs, stops, and nearby points of interest.

Caution is advised on narrow or curving roads.
amenities: Biking; Educational; Scenic Views; Farm; Water Sports

name: Tye River
description: Nestled in the heart of the Blue Ridge Mountains, the Tye River stretches 34 miles and offers an exhilarating escape for experienced canoeists. With Class I–II+ whitewater, paddlers can expect an engaging adventure amidst stunning mountain views and vibrant seasonal scenery. Ideal for those seeking both thrill and tranquility, the river features seasonal paddling windows that enhance the experience. Don't miss the scenic Lower Shamokin Falls Trail nearby, and consider stopping by Blue Mountain Brewery afterward for a refreshing reward. Embrace the beauty and excitement of the Tye River for an unforgettable outdoor experience!
image1Desc: Bridge over river surrounded by lush forest and distant hills.
address: Tye River Main Access 2724 Patrick Henry Highway Piney River VA 22964
amenities: Water Sports

name: James River
description: The James River, forming the southeastern border of Nelson County, is a haven for outdoor enthusiasts, offering a rich tapestry of experiences along Virginia's most storied waterway. Visitors can enjoy numerous canoe and kayak launches, as well as johnboat access, making it a prime spot for both serene paddles and exhilarating float trips. The river is teeming with diverse fish species, including smallmouth and largemouth bass, catfish, and sunfish, providing ample opportunities for anglers. Explore the scenic beauty of the 64-mile Upper James River Water Trail, where lush landscapes and captivating wildlife await. After a day on the water, unwind at nearby attractions like the Lower Shamokin Falls Trail or the local favorite, Blue Mountain Brewery, for a refreshing drink and a taste of the area's charm.
image1Desc: Serene river surrounded by lush green trees and distant mountains under clear sky.
accordionPanel1Content: The James River is one of Virginia’s most significant waterways and offers a wide range of recreational opportunities in Nelson County, including paddling, fishing, and scenic river access.
accordionPanel2Content: River conditions vary by section and season. Some stretches are suitable for easy, flatwater paddling, while others include moving water that requires experience and careful planning.
accordionPanel3Content: The James River supports a variety of freshwater species and attracts anglers throughout the year. Access points range from easily reached riverbanks to more remote locations.
accordionPanel4Content: Visitors should check water levels and weather conditions before heading out and follow all safety guidance. Life jackets and appropriate gear are strongly recommended.
amenities: Biking; Hiking; Water Sports; Fishing

name: Rockfish River
description: Nestled in the heart of Nelson County, the Rockfish River offers a delightful paddling experience as it meanders southeast toward the James River. Paddlers can enjoy the gentle Class I–II waters, perfect for both beginners and seasoned adventurers. The scenic routes, framed by lush landscapes, feature thrilling Class I riffles and seasonal floats that come alive with winter flows. Take out at Route 6 or explore the peaceful stretches between Routes 600 and 6, where you can pause to soak in the serene beauty. After your adventure, unwind at the nearby Blue Mountain Brewery for a refreshing drink, making your visit to Rockfish River a memorable combination of nature and relaxation.
image1Desc: Person kayaking with a dog in green kayak on a river.
address: Rockfish River Access 5156 Rockfish Valley Highway Afton VA 22920
accordionPanel1Content: The Rockfish River is a smaller tributary of the James River that flows through Nelson County and provides opportunities for fishing, paddling, and quiet river exploration.
accordionPanel2Content: The river includes calmer stretches suitable for casual recreation as well as sections where conditions change with rainfall. Water levels can fluctuate quickly.
accordionPanel3Content: Anglers visit the Rockfish River for its scenic setting and seasonal fishing opportunities. Access points vary in ease and visibility.
accordionPanel4Content: Visitors should be mindful of changing water conditions and respect private property along the river corridor.
amenities: Water Sports; Fishing

name: Lake Nelson
description: Nestled just outside Arrington, Lake Nelson is a serene 40-acre DGIF reservoir ideal for outdoor enthusiasts seeking a peaceful escape. Accessible year-round, the lake features a well-maintained concrete boat ramp, perfect for launching your electric-motor boat to explore its tranquil waters. Anglers can enjoy bank fishing or set out on their boats to catch a variety of species, including largemouth bass, crappie, channel catfish, and sunfish. Seasonal restrooms add to the convenience, making it an excellent spot for a full day of fishing or picnicking. After your adventure, consider exploring the nearby Lower Shamokin Falls Trail or stopping by the Blue Mountain Brewery for a refreshing local brew. Lake Nelson offers not just fishing, but a chance to immerse yourself in the natural beauty of Virginia's landscape.
image1Desc: Calm lake reflecting cloudy sky, surrounded by dense forest, distant mountains visible.
amenities: Water Sports; Fishing

name: Dickie Brothers Orchard
description: Nestled in the heart of Virginia’s lush countryside, Dickie Brothers Orchard stands proud as one of the state’s Century Farms, inviting visitors to experience the joy of pick-your-own adventures. From June through November, guests can wander the picturesque fields, hand-picking juicy raspberries, apples, and vibrant pumpkins, all while enjoying the fresh air and stunning views. The orchard also offers freshly pressed cider and a variety of farm-made goods, perfect for taking home a taste of the season. After your harvest, explore nearby dining options like Smokin’ Barrel Restaurant or Blue Mountain Brewery to complete your farm-to-table experience. Discover the charm of this historic orchard and create wonderful memories with family and friends!
image1Desc: Child in dress standing by Dickie Bros Orchard sign, rustic background.
image2Desc: Pumpkins and colorful flowers displayed outside rustic wooden building with American flag.
amenities: Farm; Cider; Local Ingredients; Tastings

name: Drumheller's Orchard
description: Discover the charm of Drumheller's Orchard, a family-owned gem in the heart of Virginia, where you can indulge in a selection of classic apple varieties and artisanal house-made cider. Embrace the spirit of fall during our vibrant festivals, featuring hayrides, freshly baked treats, and a welcoming environment for both pets and families. With scenic grounds perfect for leisurely afternoons and the joy of apple picking, this destination offers a delightful getaway for visitors of all ages.
image1Desc: Pink and white blossoms on a branch against a clear blue sky.
amenities: Bakery; Cider; Farm; Pet Friendly; Local Ingredients; Tastings

name: Saunders Brothers Farm Market
description: Discover the charm of Saunders Brothers Farm Market, where you can savor the freshest homegrown peaches and apples, along with a delightful selection of nursery stock. Our inviting country shop offers an array of locally sourced meats, delicious baked goods, and our famous peach ice cream, making it a perfect stop for families and food lovers alike. Join us on weekends for special events that celebrate our agricultural heritage and community spirit. Experience the warmth of farm-fresh flavors and the joy of a true country market!
image1Desc: American flag waves outside rustic store with produce sign and wooden facade.
address: 2717 Tye Brook Highway, Piney River, VA 22964
amenities: Farm; Market; Desserts; Bakery; Local Ingredients; Family Friendly; Museum; Water Sports

name: Big Arms Farm
description: Nestled in the heart of Virginia's picturesque landscape, Big Arms Farm is a vibrant market farm dedicated to educating visitors about sustainable agriculture and the joys of fresh, local produce. Known for its stunning cut flowers, heirloom vegetables, and premium grass-fed beef, the farm not only enriches the local economy but also supports global initiatives aimed at rebuilding war-torn communities. At the Nelson Farmers Market, guests can explore a delightful array of bouquets and specialty goods, making each visit a celebration of connection, community, and culinary adventure. Come discover the beauty and bounty of Big Arms Farm, where every purchase makes a difference!
image1Desc: Smiling couple under canopy surrounded by colorful flowers.
address: Nelson Farmers Market Cooperative, 868 Front Street, Lovingston, VA 22949

name: Caldwell Farms
description: Discover Caldwell Farms, a charming U-pick flower farm nestled in Stagebridge, where nature's beauty unfolds in curated seasonal blooms. By appointment only, our farm offers a unique experience with private design sessions, allowing you to create stunning floral arrangements while enjoying the serene countryside. Join us to celebrate the art of floral design and take home a piece of nature’s splendor.
image1Desc: Colorful bouquet of flowers with green fields in the background.
amenities: Seasonal Menu; Retail; Farm; Local Ingredients

name: Davis Creek Farm
description: Davis Creek Farm is a holistic, family-run operation situated on 60 acres in a pristine hollow of Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains. The farm raises heritage livestock and offers farm stays, workshops, and by-appointment experiences.
image1Desc: Horses grazing in a lush, green pasture with a forest background.
amenities: Farm; Local Ingredients

name: Deer Creek Farm
description: Nestled in the serene countryside of Lowesville, Deer Creek Farm is a charming family-run cattle and lamb farm dedicated to providing high-quality, custom meat shares. Visitors can choose from whole, half, or quarter selections of premium beef and lamb, perfect for family gatherings or special occasions. The farm's picturesque surroundings offer a glimpse into traditional farming life, making it a delightful stop on your journey through the beautiful Montebello area. Enjoy nearby attractions like the Montebello Fish Hatchery, Veritas Vineyards & Winery, and Blue Mountain Brewery, creating a perfect day of exploration and tasting in Virginia's stunning landscape.
image1Desc: Grilled steak sizzling on open flame with rosemary garnish.
amenities: Order Pickup; Farm; Local Ingredients

name: Edible Landscaping
description: Nestled in the picturesque foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains, Edible Landscaping offers a unique opportunity to immerse yourself in the world of sustainable gardening. Here, you’ll find a diverse selection of edible plants, including fruit trees, vibrant berries, climbing vines, and aromatic herbs—all cultivated without herbicides. Visitors can explore the nursery, learn about the art of edible landscaping, and discover how to bring these delicious, homegrown treasures to their own gardens. Beyond the nursery, enjoy the scenic beauty of nearby attractions like Deer Creek Farm and Veritas Vineyards, making it a perfect stop on a day of exploration in this stunning region. Whether you’re a gardening enthusiast or simply curious about sustainable practices, Edible Landscaping promises a delightful and informative experience.
image1Desc: Hand picking ripe blackberries from bush with green leaves.

name: Fitzgerald Farms
description: Fitzgerald Farms roadside stand offering summer sweet corn, fall pumpkin picking, and wholesale produce from the Rockfish Valley. Pick-Your-Own Pumpkins during the fall season and sweet corn during the summer.
image1Desc: Child sitting among numerous bright orange pumpkins, wearing pink overalls.
amenities: Farm; Desserts; Fishing

name: Fitzgerald's Orchard
description: Discover Fitzgerald's Orchard, a charming family-run farm nestled near Tyro, Virginia. Each harvest season, we proudly offer a delightful selection of classic Virginia apples, including Fuji, Rome, and Pink Lady, all handpicked for quality and flavor. Join us for a memorable experience as you explore our orchard and enjoy the beauty of the countryside, perfect for family outings and apple picking adventures.
image1Desc: Red and yellow apples on leafy tree branch under blue sky.

name: Hungry Hill Farm
description: Nestled in the heart of Virginia’s picturesque landscape, Hungry Hill Farm invites you to explore the enchanting world of beekeeping and sustainable farming. Open year-round, our farm offers a delightful range of experiences, including guided tours by appointment that reveal the fascinating life of bees. Discover our selection of raw honey and bee supplies, and join us for engaging mushroom workshops that connect you with nature. As you wander through our scenic property, take in the beauty of the surrounding area, which is dotted with local gems like Veritas Vineyards and Blue Mountain Brewery. Whether you’re a nature enthusiast or simply looking for a unique outing, Hungry Hill Farm is a sweet escape you won’t want to miss!
image1Desc: Bee sipping liquid from glass rim, close-up, detailed, blurred background.
amenities: Farm; Retail

name: Lost Point Farm
description: Nestled above the serene Tye River, Lost Point Farm is a charming small herb and produce farm dedicated to providing the Arrington community with fresh, chemical-free harvests. Visitors can schedule appointments to explore the farm’s vibrant fields, where they can witness the careful cultivation of a variety of herbs and seasonal produce. Enjoy the peaceful surroundings and perhaps pair your visit with nearby attractions like Veritas Vineyards & Winery or Blue Mountain Brewery for a delightful day of local flavors and natural beauty. Whether you're stocking up on farm-fresh ingredients or simply soaking in the tranquil atmosphere, Lost Point Farm offers a unique glimpse into sustainable farming practices in the heart of Virginia's picturesque countryside.
image1Desc: White flowers in front of wooden cabin surrounded by lush greenery.
amenities: Order Pickup; Scenic Views; Farm; Local Ingredients; Water Sports

name: Pharsalia
description: Discover the historic Pharsalia estate, built in 1814 by William Massie, nestled in the picturesque landscape of Nelson County, Virginia. This stunning venue offers breathtaking views, charming gardens, and original outbuildings, making it an ideal setting for weddings, group tours, and floral workshops. Immerse yourself in the beauty of our working orchards while experiencing the rich heritage of this remarkable property.
image1Desc: White house surrounded by colorful trees, with mountains in the background.
accordionPanel1Content: Pharsalia is a historic hilltop estate overlooking the Rockfish Valley. The property is known for its architecture, long history, and expansive views of the surrounding countryside.
accordionPanel2Content: The estate dates to the early 19th century and reflects the agricultural and social history of the region. Over time, the property has served a variety of cultural and community roles.
accordionPanel3Content: Public access to Pharsalia is limited and typically associated with scheduled events or special openings.

name: Robinia Institute
description: Nestled within the breathtaking Timshel Wildland, the Robinia Institute invites visitors to explore the transformative world of regenerative agriculture on its expansive 400-acre conservation site. Here, guests can participate in hands-on grazing intensives and engage in educational workshops that highlight sustainable farming practices. Surrounded by the serene beauty of Inglewood Farm and the vibrant ecosystems of nearby Montebello Fish Hatchery, the institute serves as a vital hub for those passionate about environmental stewardship. Whether you're a novice or a seasoned farmer, Robinia Institute offers a unique opportunity to learn and connect with nature, making it a must-visit destination for eco-conscious travelers.
image1Desc: Person in hat tending plants in a lush green field.

name: Rose Isle Farm
description: Rose Isle Farm collaborates with a local brewery to produce premium 'beer-fed' beef, enhancing sustainable practices in animal husbandry. By utilizing spent mash from the brewery, the farm creates a unique and eco-friendly approach to cattle raising. Visitors can enjoy direct sales of this exceptional beef by appointment, showcasing the harmonious blend of local agriculture and craft brewing in Nelson County. Experience the taste of innovation and sustainability at Rose Isle Farm.
image1Desc: Farm with silo, red roofs, green fields, and hazy mountains in the background.
amenities: Beer; Farm; Local Ingredients; Tastings

name: Seamans' Orchard
description: Tucked away at the foot of the stunning Blue Ridge Mountains, Seamans' Orchard is a cherished fourth-generation family farm that promises a delightful experience for all visitors. Here, nature's bounty flourishes, with the farm offering a vibrant selection of apples, blueberries, cherries, and strawberries—all lovingly nurtured for the finest flavors. As you stroll through the picturesque orchards, take in the breathtaking mountain views and enjoy seasonal picking events that are perfect for families. After your visit, explore nearby culinary gems like Smokin’ Barrel Restaurant or indulge in artisan treats at Fire & Frost Wood Fired Bakehouse, making for a perfect day of local flavors and farm-fresh goodness.
image1Desc: Cherries, blueberries, strawberries in clear containers on a wooden table.
amenities: Farm; Market; Scenic Views; Family Friendly

name: Silver Creek and Seamans' Orchards
description: Nestled in the heart of the scenic countryside, Silver Creek and Seamans' Orchards invites visitors to indulge in a delightful array of heirloom apple varieties, including Empire, Gala, Jonathan, and Pink Lady. Their charming packing shed is not just a place to purchase fresh produce; it’s a hub for cider lovers, apple butter enthusiasts, and those looking for local honey and pumpkins. After exploring the orchards, enjoy a meal at the Smokin’ Barrel Restaurant or savor wood-fired specialties at Fire & Frost Bakehouse. Whether you're picking your own apples or simply enjoying the picturesque views, this family-friendly destination promises a memorable experience for all ages.
image1Desc: Crates of colorful apples displayed inside a rustic market setting.
amenities: Cider; Local Ingredients; Events; Farm; Tastings

name: Silver Creek Orchards
description: Silver Creek Orchards is a seventh-generation family-owned farm that offers over 20 varieties of pick-your-own apples, along with wine grapes and beef cattle. Visitors can enjoy scenic mountain views on select weekends.
image1Desc: Crates filled with red apples in sunlight, stacked outdoors.
amenities: Farm; Family Friendly; Scenic Views; Events

name: Silver Fox Lavender Farm
description: Experience the enchanting charm of Silver Fox Lavender Farm, nestled amidst the scenic beauty of Silver Creek. Each June, the farm bursts into a vibrant tapestry of purple during our annual Lavender Festival. Visitors can immerse themselves in the fragrant fields, participate in engaging farm workshops, and unwind with rejuvenating yoga sessions. Our picturesque barn venue is perfect for intimate micro weddings and special events. After exploring, indulge in delightful culinary offerings nearby at Smokin’ Barrel Restaurant, Giuseppe’s, or Fire & Frost Wood Fired Bakehouse. Join us for a unique blend of nature, community, and celebration!
image1Desc: Barn and field under cloudy sky with mountain in background.
amenities: Events; Farm; Retail

name: The Apple Shed
description: Discover a delightful selection of fresh, locally grown apples and pumpkins at The Apple Shed. Our farm invites you to pick your own produce, ensuring a fun and memorable experience for families and friends alike. Enjoy seasonal activities, farm tours, and the chance to learn about sustainable farming practices. Join us for a taste of the harvest and create lasting memories in the heart of nature.
image1Desc: Red sign with white apple design, text reads 'The Apple Shed.'
amenities: Market; Seasonal Menu; Local Ingredients; Farm

accordionPanel1Content:
History

The Blue Ridge Tunnel was designed by French-born engineer Claudius Crozet (1789–1864), one of the most influential transportation engineers of the 19th century. A graduate of the École Polytechnique in Paris, Crozet later taught engineering at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point and helped found the Virginia Military Institute.

As chief engineer, Crozet surveyed a rail route through Rockfish Gap to connect eastern and western Virginia. His plan included several tunnels, extensive embankments, and the nearly one-mile-long Blue Ridge Tunnel between Nelson and Augusta counties.

Construction proved far more difficult than expected due to extremely hard rock, particularly greenstone. Despite these challenges, Irish immigrant laborers successfully bored through the mountain, meeting with remarkable precision in December 1856.

The tunnel opened to rail traffic on April 13, 1858, becoming the longest railroad tunnel in North America at the time. Although Crozet had resigned shortly before its completion, his engineering vision was essential to the project’s success.

Learn more about the tunnel’s history at the Blue Ridge Tunnel Foundation.
accordionPanel2Content:
Trail & Park Rules

The Blue Ridge Tunnel Trail is open daily from sunrise to sunset. Visitors should remain aware of other trail users, watch for uneven ground inside the tunnel, and bring flashlights or headlamps at all times.

Trailhead parking areas are small and limited. When parking areas are full, the trail is considered full. Visitors should park only in designated spaces and never along roadways. There is no overnight parking, RV parking, or camping at either trailhead.

For a less strenuous experience, including improved accessibility for wheelchair users, the east trailhead is recommended. Cyclists are also encouraged to use the east side and must always yield to pedestrians.

Help protect the natural environment by staying on designated trails and avoiding damage to plants, trees, and wildlife. Collecting plants or animals is prohibited, and visitors should pack out all trash. Feeding wildlife and releasing balloons are not allowed.

Mountain bikes are permitted only on designated roads. The use of motorized vehicles, drones, fireworks, and unmanned aircraft is prohibited. Alcohol use is not permitted, and smoking is not allowed inside the tunnel.

Overnight camping is prohibited and considered trespassing. All visitors are expected to follow Virginia law while using the trail.
accordionPanel3Content:
Trail Conditions & What to Expect

Distance & Time

At a comfortable walking pace, a hike to the western portal and back typically takes about 1.5 hours. The trail is approximately 2.25 miles one way and 4.5 miles round trip when walking from one trailhead to the other and returning.

Trail Surface

The trail is primarily crushed gravel with some steep inclines. Inside the tunnel, the surface may be uneven due to ruts and puddles caused by constant water drip.

Lighting & Visibility

The tunnel is not lit and is very dark. A high-powered flashlight or headlamp is strongly recommended for all visitors.

Weather & Clothing

The interior of the tunnel remains cool year-round, typically between 55–65°F. Water drips continuously from the ceiling and walls, so visitors should wear appropriate clothing and sturdy, comfortable shoes.

Wet Areas & Stream Crossing

Puddles are common inside the tunnel. On the west side of the trail, a concrete stream crossing may have water flowing over it during or after rainstorms. Use caution in wet conditions.

Facilities

Portable restrooms are available at both the eastern and western parking areas but are not located along the trail. There are no water fountains on the trail, so visitors should bring drinking water.
accordionPanel4Content:
Frequently Asked Questions

Is the trail suitable for wheelchairs?

The trail surface is crushed gravel. The east trail has minimal elevation change and is generally the most accessible option. The tunnel is unlit and remains cool year-round (approximately 55–65°F), with constant water dripping that can create puddles and ruts. Visitors should consider these conditions when planning their visit.

Trail grades and accessibility details

East Trail to Tunnel Entrance: 0.63 miles with a gentle average grade of approximately 1.5%.

Tunnel: Approximately 4,273 feet long with a gradual average grade of 1.3%.

West Trail to Tunnel Entrance: Steeper terrain with sustained grades over 5% and a maximum grade of approximately 19%. This section is more challenging.

Are dogs allowed?

Yes. Dogs are permitted on the trail and in the tunnel but must be kept on a leash at all times. Owners are responsible for cleaning up after their pets.

How long is the trail and tunnel?

The full trail from one trailhead to the other is approximately 2.25 miles. The tunnel itself is nearly one mile long.

From the east trailhead through the tunnel: approximately 1.44 miles. From the west trailhead through the tunnel: approximately 1.62 miles.

Who manages the trail?

The trail and tunnel are owned by Nelson County and maintained by the Nelson County Parks and Recreation Department.

Are restrooms or amenities available?

Portable restrooms are located at both the east and west trailheads. There are no restrooms or water fountains along the trail.

What are the visiting hours?

The trail and tunnel are open daily from sunrise to sunset.

Is the tunnel lit?

No. Visitors must bring high-powered flashlights or headlamps to safely travel through the tunnel.

Can I ride a bike on the trail?

Yes. Cyclists are encouraged to use the east trail, which has gentler grades. The west trail is steeper and best suited for experienced riders. Bicyclists must yield to pedestrians and be prepared for wet, uneven conditions inside the tunnel.

accordionPanel1Content:
Crabtree Falls is one of the most well-known waterfall hikes in Virginia, featuring a series of cascading waterfalls that descend more than 1,200 feet along the eastern slope of the Blue Ridge Mountains. The trail follows Crabtree Creek through a steep, wooded gorge and offers multiple designated viewpoints of the falls.

The site is managed as a protected natural area and is valued for both its scenic beauty and its challenging terrain.
accordionPanel2Content:
The main trail to Crabtree Falls is approximately 3 miles round-trip and is considered strenuous. The route is steep and rocky, with uneven footing, exposed roots, and narrow sections along the gorge.

Elevation gain is significant, especially on the return hike uphill, and the trail requires good physical condition and sturdy footwear.
accordionPanel3Content:
Crabtree Falls has a history of serious accidents, often caused by visitors leaving the marked trail or climbing on wet rocks near the water. Staying on designated paths and observing posted warnings is essential.

Visitors should never attempt to climb the falls or cross barriers placed for safety.
accordionPanel4Content:
Due to the difficulty of the trail, Crabtree Falls is best suited for experienced hikers. Visitors should allow adequate time for the hike, carry water, and be prepared for changing weather conditions.

Practicing Leave No Trace principles helps protect both visitors and the natural environment.

The preserve is managed for conservation and low-impact recreation.
accordionPanel2Content:
Trails within the preserve range from moderate to strenuous and include rocky terrain, elevation changes, and river views.

Routes vary in length and can be combined for longer hikes.
accordionPanel3Content:
Because of steep terrain and natural hazards, visitors should remain on designated trails and follow posted guidance.

Practicing Leave No Trace principles helps protect sensitive habitats.
accordionPanel4Content: The preserve is best suited for experienced hikers. Visitors should plan ahead, bring adequate supplies, and be prepared for limited facilities.
amenities: Hiking; Biking

name: Fortune's Ridge Trail
description: Explore the enchanting Fortune's Ridge Trail, a scenic 1.1-mile path adorned with vibrant red blazes. This picturesque trail meanders alongside the serene Fortunes Ridge stream, showcasing captivating cascades and seasonal laurel blooms. Accessible from both Fortunes Ridge and Wintergreen Drive, it's the perfect destination for nature lovers and outdoor enthusiasts seeking a peaceful retreat amidst stunning natural beauty. Whether you're hiking solo or with family, Fortune's Ridge Trail promises an unforgettable experience in the heart of the wilderness.
image1Desc: Wooden trail sign reads 'Laurel Ridge Loop 3 Mile' in forest.
amenities: Scenic Views; Biking; Hiking; Water Sports

name: Hemlock Springs Loop
description: Hemlock Springs Loop is a 0.8-mile trail near Wintergreen, featuring pink and yellow lady's slippers and remnants of old-growth hemlocks affected by woolly adelgid. This yellow-red loop includes moderate climbs and requires careful navigation due to its sensitive habitat.
image1Desc: Person standing on large rock surrounded by green grass.
amenities: Hiking; Biking

name: Highlands Leisure Trail
description: Discover the Highlands Leisure Trail, a scenic 0.5-mile path that links Wintergreen's Blackrock Village to the Wintergarden. This enchanting trail meanders through a lush, older-growth forest and features a stunning overlook of the Highlands ski slopes. Ideal for hikers of all levels, it offers short climbs that reward you with breathtaking views and a serene natural atmosphere. Experience the beauty of the Virginia mountains as you explore this charming trail.
image1Desc: Wooded trail with steps surrounded by lush green foliage and sunlight.
amenities: Scenic Views; Resort; Biking; Hiking

name: Humpback Rocks
description: Humpback Rocks offers a rewarding 2-mile loop climb featuring 360-degree views of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Starting from the visitor center near Parkway milepost 5.8, expect a 45-minute ascent and a 20-minute descent, gaining 740 feet in elevation.
image1Desc: Sunrise over misty valley with rocky foreground and scattered clouds.
address: Humpback Gap Parking Area, Milepost 5.8 Blue Ridge Parkway, Lyndhurst, VA 22952
accordionPanel1Content:
Humpback Rocks is one of the most popular hiking destinations in the Blue Ridge Mountains, known for its dramatic rock outcrop and sweeping views of the Shenandoah Valley and surrounding ridgelines.

The summit provides one of the most recognizable viewpoints along the Blue Ridge Parkway.
accordionPanel2Content:
The primary trail to Humpback Rocks is approximately 2 miles round-trip and is considered strenuous due to its steep climb and rocky steps.

Although the distance is short, the elevation gain is significant and requires good physical conditioning.
accordionPanel3Content: The summit area includes exposed rock and steep drop-offs. Visitors should use caution near edges and be mindful of weather conditions, particularly high winds or wet surfaces.
accordionPanel4Content: Because of its popularity, Humpback Rocks can be busy during peak seasons. Arriving early and wearing sturdy footwear can help ensure a safer and more enjoyable hike.
amenities: Scenic Views; Biking; Hiking

name: James River State Park
description: Discover the natural beauty of James River State Park, where over 15 miles of multiuse trails wind through scenic landscapes. Enjoy breathtaking riverfront overlooks, perfect for picnicking or taking in the views. The park features convenient boat launches for kayaking and canoeing, along with cozy cabins for a relaxing stay. Experience a full-service canoe livery that caters to all your paddling needs, making this destination ideal for outdoor enthusiasts and families alike. Come explore the wonders of the James River!
image1Desc: Stone entrance sign reading 'James River Wildlife Management Area' among trees.
accordionPanel1Content: James River State Park is a large public park that offers access to the James River along with forests, open meadows, and scenic overlooks. The park protects a diverse landscape while providing space for outdoor recreation and quiet exploration.
accordionPanel2Content: The park includes a network of hiking and biking trails ranging from easy riverside walks to moderate upland routes with elevation changes. River access supports paddling and fishing, and open areas are suitable for picnicking and wildlife viewing.
accordionPanel3Content: Because of the park’s size, visitors can choose from short outings or full-day adventures. Trails are well-marked, and different areas of the park offer distinct experiences depending on interest and ability.
accordionPanel4Content: Visitors should review maps and trail descriptions in advance and allow sufficient time to explore. Conditions can vary by season, particularly along river corridors.
amenities: Boating; Cabins; Water Sports; Biking; Hiking

name: Kids in Parks: Virginia Blue Ridge Railway Trail
description: Embark on a delightful adventure at the Virginia Blue Ridge Railway Trail, a family-friendly TRACK Trail located at the scenic Piney River Depot. This flat, accessible rail-trail invites young explorers to engage with nature through self-guided activities that spark curiosity and learning. As you stroll along the picturesque path, keep an eye out for local wildlife and enjoy the stunning mountain views. Kids can earn exciting prizes through the Kids in Parks program, making each hike a rewarding experience. Perfect for families looking to connect with nature, this trail offers a wonderful way to create lasting memories together amidst the beauty of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
image1Desc: Wooden covered bridge over forest path; red bicycle leaning nearby.
address: 3124 Patrick Henry Highway, Piney River, VA 22964
accordionPanel1Content: This Kids in Parks trail follows portions of the Virginia Blue Ridge Railway corridor, offering a gentle outdoor experience tied to local history.
accordionPanel2Content: The trail is considered easy and is well suited for children, families, and casual walkers.
accordionPanel3Content: Families can participate in self-guided activities that encourage exploration and learning along the trail.
amenities: Hiking; Adventure; Family Friendly; Parking; Biking; Water Sports; Hunting

name: HeartRock Retreat & Homestead
description: Fifteen-acre Heart Rock homestead with lodging for up to 15, edible gardens, and retreat spaces minutes from breweries and river access. Located in Nelson County, Virginia, our fifteen acre homestead offers both rustic charm and modern comfort. Nelson County has something for everyone.
image1Desc: Lush green garden with various plants and trees in a forest setting.
image2Desc: Lush vegetable garden with rows, greenhouses, surrounded by trees under cloudy sky.
image3Desc: Bee collecting nectar from honey on shiny surface.
amenities: Outdoor Seating; Beer; Organic; Farm; Local Ingredients; Water Sports

name: Laurel Ridge Loop
description: Discover the beauty of the Laurel Ridge Loop, a scenic 1.6-mile trail that meanders through a stunning landscape of mountain laurel, birch, and oak-hickory forests. With its rocky terrain, this yellow loop offers an invigorating hike for nature enthusiasts and outdoor explorers alike. Conveniently located with parking available at Wintergreen's Lot F, it’s the perfect spot to immerse yourself in the tranquility of nature and enjoy the vibrant flora that surrounds you. Experience the charm of the Blue Ridge Mountains on this captivating trail.
image1Desc: Wooden trail sign with yellow and red text in forest setting.
accordionPanel1Content: The Laurel Ridge Loop is a wooded hiking trail that travels along ridgelines through dense mountain vegetation. It offers a longer, more immersive forest experience.
accordionPanel2Content: The loop covers several miles and is generally considered moderate to strenuous due to elevation changes and uneven terrain.
accordionPanel3Content: Because the trail passes through remote forest, hikers should carry water, allow adequate time to complete the loop, and be prepared for limited cell service.
amenities: Hiking; Parking; Biking

name: Inglewood Fine Meats
description: Experience the essence of farm-to-table at Inglewood Fine Meats, where we take pride in offering Verified All Natural beef and lamb sourced from animals that live a quality life in the picturesque foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Nestled in the serene surroundings of Nelson County, our meats reflect the rich landscape and sustainable farming practices of the region. Visitors can expect a warm, inviting atmosphere and knowledgeable staff ready to share the story behind each cut. Pair your selections with local wines from Veritas Vineyards & Winery or a refreshing brew from Blue Mountain Brewery for the ultimate culinary journey in this enchanting area.
image1Desc: Raw meat on wooden board with garlic, chili, peppercorns, and rosemary.
amenities: Farm; Local Ingredients

name: Lower Shamokin Falls Trail
description: Discover the Lower Shamokin Falls Trail, a 1.7-mile blue-blazed path that winds through a lush forest and ends at the beautiful Lower Shamokin Falls. Starting from Old Stoney Creek Road, this trail combines jeep-road access with natural scenery, making it suitable for hikers of all skill levels. Enjoy the tranquility of nature and the soothing sounds of cascading water on this picturesque route.
image1Desc: Trail sign on tree reads 'Lower Shamokin Falls Trail' in lush forest.
amenities: Hiking; Biking; Water Sports

name: Mau-Har Trail
description: Experience the breathtaking Mau-Har Trail, a scenic three-mile connector nestled within the stunning Three Ridges Wilderness. This captivating route links to the iconic Appalachian Trail, guiding you past cascading waterfalls, challenging rock scrambles, and cozy shelters. Perfect for outdoor enthusiasts, the trail offers an exhilarating adventure through nature’s beauty, making it a must-visit for hikers seeking a memorable journey.
image1Desc: Small waterfall cascading over rocks surrounded by autumn foliage.
address: Blue Ridge Parkway Milepost 13.7, Roseland, VA 22967
accordionPanel1Content:
The Mau-Har Trail is a scenic backcountry hiking route in the George Washington National Forest, known for its waterfalls, stream crossings, and forested mountain terrain.

The trail is often used as part of a loop hike that includes the nearby Appalachian Trail.
accordionPanel2Content:
The Mau-Har Trail is approximately 3 miles one way and is considered moderate to strenuous. The route follows a creek corridor with multiple stream crossings and includes steady elevation change.

Footing can be rocky and uneven, particularly after rain.
accordionPanel3Content:
Stream crossings may be difficult during periods of high water. Visitors should use caution, especially after heavy rainfall.

Because this is a backcountry trail, preparation and navigation awareness are important.
accordionPanel4Content: Hikers should carry sufficient water, wear sturdy footwear, and allow adequate time for the hike. Checking weather conditions before starting is strongly recommended.
amenities: Hiking; Biking; Appalachian Trail; Water Sports

name: Montebello Nature Trail
description: Embark on a serene half-mile nature walk along the enchanting Montebello Nature Trail, nestled beside the remnants of a former fish hatchery stream. As you meander through this picturesque landscape, you'll be greeted by lush fern-lined banks and the melodic songs of various bird species, offering a delightful auditory backdrop. Along the trail, benches invite you to pause and soak in the tranquil surroundings. This easy stroll is perfect for families and nature enthusiasts alike, providing a peaceful escape into the heart of nature. Don’t forget your camera to capture the beauty of this hidden gem!
image1Desc: People walking on a sunny forest trail surrounded by green trees.
amenities: Biking; Hiking; Water Sports; Fishing

name: Nelson County Wilderness Area
description: Discover the breathtaking beauty of the Nelson County Wilderness Area, where the majestic Priest and Three Ridges offer an unforgettable hiking experience. Explore rugged trails along the Appalachian Trail, featuring dramatic elevation changes that reward adventurers with stunning vistas and a sense of solitude in nature. Whether you're seeking a challenging trek or a peaceful retreat, this protected wilderness area invites you to immerse yourself in the tranquility of the great outdoors.
image1Desc: Hiker with a green backpack walking through a forest.
address: George Washington National Forest, Montebello, VA 24464
amenities: Hiking; Biking; Appalachian Trail; Water Sports

name: North Fork of the Piney River
description: Explore the tranquil North Fork of the Piney River, where lush landscapes meet serene waters. Follow Route 666 past Dickie Brothers Orchard into George Washington National Forest. This picturesque area is ideal for picnics under towering trees and offers a peaceful retreat for nature lovers. Whether hiking or enjoying the scenery, the North Fork provides an unforgettable outdoor experience.
image1Desc: Water cascading over mossy rocks surrounded by green leaves.
amenities: Water Sports; Biking; Hiking; Farm; Fishing; Swimming Pool

name: Old Appalachian Trail
description: Moderate-to-difficult grades reward hikers with Shenandoah Valley vistas and quiet, historic tread. 3.3-mile former Appalachian Trail alignment with greenstone ledges, Shenandoah Valley overlooks, and spring wildflowers across multiple access points.
image1Desc: Narrow dirt path with yellow moss, surrounded by trees in a forest.
amenities: Hiking; Biking; Appalachian Trail

name: Paul's Creek Trail
description: Paul's Creek Trail is a 0.6-mile blue-blazed family favorite that follows a lush valley to smooth rock chutes and a series of cascading waterfalls near Crawford's Knob. Pack water shoes and a camera—the polished boulders and cool pools are irresistible on summer days.
image1Desc: Forest stream flowing over rocks surrounded by trees and autumn leaves.
amenities: Family Friendly; Biking; Hiking; Water Sports; Swimming Pool

name: Pedlars Edge Trail
description: Discover the Pedlars Edge Trail, a challenging 1.6-mile red trail that winds alongside the stunning Blackrock formation. This captivating hike offers a unique blend of geology and biodiversity, showcasing the remarkable pedlar formation rocks. As you traverse the trail, enjoy expansive views of open powerline areas, perfect for birdwatching, while vibrant wildflower habitats add bursts of color to your journey. Ideal for adventurous nature enthusiasts, this trail promises an unforgettable outdoor experience.
image1Desc: Bird perched on icy branch, blue sky background.
amenities: Biking; Hiking

name: Pond Hollow Trail
description: Discover the captivating Pond Hollow Trail, a challenging one-mile trek that meanders through a stunning landscape of displaced boulders and diverse plant communities. This unique route offers an opportunity to explore prime bobcat habitat while enjoying the natural beauty of the surrounding area. Perfect for adventurous hikers, the trail's vibrant ecosystem and geological features create an unforgettable outdoor experience.
image1Desc: Group of people walking through lush green forest near rocky cliff.
amenities: Biking; Hiking

name: Ravens Roost Park
description: 0.5-mile yellow loop through mixed forest with wildflower displays, solitude, and access from White Oak Drive or Wintergreen Drive. Ravens Roost Park offers a half-mile yellow-blazed wander through deep forest to a favorite Skyline Drive overlook for sunrise, sunset, and wildflower spotting.
image1Desc: Wooden deck overlooks vast green forest landscape and distant horizon.
amenities: Seasonal Menu; Hiking; Biking

name: Shamokin Springs Nature Preserve
description: Discover the serene beauty of Shamokin Springs Nature Preserve, a 0.3-mile loop that showcases pristine high-elevation wetlands and enchanting braided streams. This family-friendly trail is home to a diverse array of northern plant species, making it a perfect spot for nature enthusiasts and casual hikers alike. Enjoy easy access to breathtaking landscapes and immerse yourself in the tranquility of this protected environment. Whether you're seeking a leisurely stroll or a chance to connect with nature, Shamokin Springs invites you to explore its unique ecosystem.
image1Desc: Small waterfall cascading over rocks in a forest stream.
image2Desc: Mountain landscape with distant green hills and scattered clouds beneath blue sky.
amenities: Educational; Family Friendly; Biking; Hiking

name: The Plunge
description: Discover The Plunge, a scenic 0.2-mile connector to the Blackrock Trail that offers a thrilling adventure for nature lovers. This short but steep hike showcases stunning pedlar gneiss rock formations and breathtaking panoramic views, making it an ideal spot for capturing family memories. With its picturesque overlooks and unique geological features, The Plunge invites you to experience the beauty of the outdoors in a captivating way.
image1Desc: Rocky viewpoint overlooking lush, green mountains under clear blue sky.
amenities: Family Friendly; Biking; Hiking

name: Trillium Field
description: Trillium Field offers a delightful 0.1-mile trail adorned with vibrant white and pink trillium blossoms each May. Located at the intersection of Wintergreen Drive and Devils Knob Loop, this scenic spot transforms into a wildflower haven throughout the summer months. Perfect for a leisurely walk, it's an inviting escape for nature lovers and photographers alike. Discover the beauty of this charming trail and immerse yourself in a seasonal spectacle.
image1Desc: Pink and white flowers with green leaves in a forest setting.
amenities: Seasonal Menu; Biking; Hiking

name: Upper Shamokin Falls Trail
description: Upper Shamokin Falls Trail is a gentle 0.4-mile walk that follows the sound of tumbling water to fern-draped cascades—perfect for all ages. Stay on the marked path and off the slick rock edges, but don't forget the camera for this signature Wintergreen scene.
image1Desc: Waterfall cascading over moss-covered rocks, surrounded by lush green forest.
amenities: Family Friendly; Hiking; Biking; Water Sports

name: Upper Shamokin Gorge Trail
description: Embark on an adventurous journey along the Upper Shamokin Gorge Trail, a challenging 0.8-mile red trail that promises an unforgettable hiking experience. As you navigate stream crossings and immerse yourself in the lush understory, you'll find yourself surrounded by the natural beauty of the gorge. This trail not only offers a thrilling hike but also connects to the iconic Appalachian Trail, making it a perfect spot for both seasoned hikers and nature enthusiasts. Discover the serenity and stunning landscapes that await you on this remarkable trail.
image1Desc: Flowing stream through forest with rocks and autumn foliage.
amenities: Hiking; Biking; Appalachian Trail; Water Sports

name: White Oak Trail
description: Immerse yourself in the serene beauty of the White Oak Trail, a charming half-mile loop nestled between White Oak Drive and Wintergreen Drive. This moderate yellow trail invites you to wander through shaded woods teeming with vibrant spring wildflowers and the soothing sounds of nature. As you explore, keep an eye out for a variety of bird species flitting among the trees—perfect for birdwatchers and nature enthusiasts alike. Whether you’re seeking a peaceful stroll or a quick escape into the wild, the White Oak Trail offers a delightful experience just a stone's throw away from the delightful offerings of nearby Blue Mountain Brewery.
image1Desc: Trail sign surrounded by lush green foliage in misty forest.
amenities: Seasonal Menu; Hiking; Biking

name: White Rock Falls
description: White Rock Falls is a 2.5-mile moderate hike along the Blue Ridge Parkway that showcases an impressive gorge, a wading-friendly waterfall, and northeast-facing mountain views on the climb out. 2.5-mile moderate waterfall hike with natural wading pools, gorge views, and options to extend via the Slacks Overlook loop on the Parkway.
image1Desc: Small waterfall flowing down rocky terrain surrounded by trees.
address: Blue Ridge Parkway Milepost 19, Montebello, VA 24464
accordionPanel1Content:
White Rock Falls is a scenic waterfall located in the Blue Ridge Mountains, reached by a forested hiking trail. The falls cascade over exposed rock, creating a striking natural feature that varies with seasonal water flow.

The area is quieter and less developed than some nearby waterfall destinations.
accordionPanel2Content:
The hike to White Rock Falls is relatively short but considered moderate to strenuous due to rocky footing, elevation changes, and stream crossings.

While the distance is manageable, hikers should expect uneven terrain and steady climbing.
accordionPanel3Content:
Trail conditions can change with weather and rainfall, making rocks and stream crossings slippery. Sturdy footwear is recommended.

Visitors should remain on the established trail to reduce risk and protect the surrounding environment.
amenities: Pool; Biking; Hiking; Water Sports

name: Three Ridges
description: The 13.3-mile Three Ridges loop is one of Virginia's premier backpacking routes, delivering waterfalls, rocky knife-edge climbs, and big Appalachian vistas south of Wintergreen. Expect strenuous terrain, overnight camping zones, and bragging rights after tackling this rugged circuit.
image1Desc: Small waterfall flowing over rocks, surrounded by autumn leaves and trees.
address: Reeds Gap Trailhead, Route 664, Roseland, VA 22967
amenities: Hiking; Biking; Appalachian Trail; Water Sports

name: Stoney Creek Park
description: Experience the serene beauty of Stoney Creek Park, a community linear park designed for families and nature lovers. Stroll along the picturesque creekside path that winds through lush landscapes, and take advantage of the newly established picnic areas and comfortable benches for relaxation. With gentle terrain and inviting surroundings, this park is perfect for leisurely walks and quality time spent outdoors. Embrace the tranquility and charm that await, making every visit a refreshing escape into nature.
image1Desc: White flowers blooming among lush green leaves in a forest setting.
address: Stoney Creek West Drive, Nellysford, VA 22958
amenities: Picnic Area; Family Friendly; Parking; Biking; Hiking

name: Spy Rock
description: Spy Rock's granite dome is accessible via a 6.5-mile round-trip hike from Meadows Lane (SR 826) following the closure of the fish hatchery lot. This route includes sustained climbs, rocky scrambles, and impressive summit views.
image1Desc: Hikers standing on rocky summit under cloudy blue sky, overlooking green mountains.
accordionPanel1Content: Spy Rock is a popular hiking destination known for its expansive summit views of the Blue Ridge Mountains. The trail leads to a large rocky outcrop that provides panoramic vistas across Nelson County and surrounding areas.
accordionPanel2Content:
The most commonly used route to Spy Rock is approximately 5 miles round-trip and is considered moderate to strenuous. The trail includes steady elevation gain, rocky sections, and uneven footing.

The final approach to the summit requires scrambling over exposed rock.
accordionPanel3Content: The summit area is exposed, and weather conditions can change quickly. Visitors should use caution near cliff edges and avoid hiking during storms or high winds.
accordionPanel4Content: Hikers should carry sufficient water, wear sturdy footwear, and allow adequate time for the hike. Staying on the established trail helps protect the landscape and ensures a safer experience.
amenities: Biking; Fishing; Hiking; Scenic Views

name: Spruce Creek Park
description: Nestled along Route 151, Spruce Creek Park serves as the vibrant heart of the Rockfish Valley Loop Trail system, inviting outdoor enthusiasts to explore its scenic beauty from sunrise to sunset. Visitors can meander along TRACK trails, discover a lush native plant garden, and immerse themselves in the tranquility of the butterfly walk. For geology buffs, the park features an enlightening geology trail, while the Rockfish Valley Foundation Natural History Center offers fascinating insights into the area's natural heritage. Don't miss the nearby Lower Shamokin Falls Trail for an additional adventure, and consider stopping by Blue Mountain Brewery or Basic Necessities for a delightful meal after your exploration.
image1Desc: Tall green thistles with spiky leaves against dense forest backdrop.
accordionPanel1Content: Spruce Creek Park is a small community park that provides access to open green space along Spruce Creek. It is designed for casual outdoor use and quiet recreation.
accordionPanel2Content: Walking paths and open areas make the park suitable for short strolls and relaxed outdoor activities. Terrain is generally easy and accessible.
accordionPanel3Content: Visitors are encouraged to respect the natural setting and follow posted guidelines to help maintain the park for community use.
amenities: Hiking; Biking; Fishing

name: Rockfish Valley Loop Trails
description: Explore the scenic Rockfish Valley Loop Trails, a flat four-mile network offering picturesque views of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Wander along well-maintained paths that meander through lush landscapes, featuring birdwatching hotspots and informative interpretive signage. This serene route, tracing the peaceful banks of the Rockfish River and Reid's Creek, beautifully combines nature and history, making it an ideal destination for outdoor enthusiasts and families alike.
image1Desc: Wooden footbridge crossing over rocky ground, surrounded by lush green trees.
address: Rockfish Valley Loop Trailhead, 1368 Rockfish Valley Highway, Nellysford, VA 22958
accordionPanel1Content:
The Rockfish Valley Loop Trails are a connected network of hiking paths that wind through forests, open fields, and stream corridors in the Rockfish Valley.

The system offers multiple loop options rather than a single out-and-back route.
accordionPanel2Content:
Individual loops range from short walks under one mile to longer routes of several miles. Overall difficulty is generally easy to moderate, depending on the route selected.

Terrain includes gentle elevation changes and well-defined paths.
accordionPanel3Content:
Because the trails interconnect, visitors are encouraged to review posted maps before starting.

Staying on marked paths helps protect surrounding land and ensures a safe experience.
amenities: Hiking; Educational; Biking; Farm; Water Sports; Fishing

name: Quarry Gardens at Schuyler
description: Discover the enchanting Quarry Gardens at Schuyler, a stunning 40-acre oasis where restored soapstone quarries have been transformed into vibrant native plant gardens. Explore two miles of scenic trails that wind through diverse habitat galleries, offering a unique opportunity to connect with nature. Join our guided ecology tours to learn about the rich biodiversity and the ecological significance of this remarkable landscape. Whether you're a nature enthusiast or simply seeking a peaceful escape, the Quarry Gardens promise an unforgettable experience.
image1Desc: Rocky cliffside and trees reflected in a calm, clear lake.
amenities: Biking; Hiking

name: Kids in Parks: Rockfish River Trailhead
description: Discover the Kids in Parks Rockfish River Trailhead, where a picturesque one-mile loop offers families a unique opportunity to explore nature together. This self-guided trail features engaging story walk signage and showcases diverse riparian habitats, making it perfect for young adventurers. Enjoy a flat, accessible route that invites children and parents alike to connect with the great outdoors along the scenic Blue Ridge Parkway.
image1Desc: Bare trees by a flowing stream, mountain and clear sky in background.
address: Rockfish River Trailhead, 1368 Rockfish Valley Highway, Nellysford, VA 22958
accordionPanel1Content: The Kids in Parks Rockfish River Trailhead is part of a family-focused program designed to encourage children and families to explore nature together.
accordionPanel2Content: Routes accessed from this trailhead are easy and family-friendly, with relatively flat terrain and manageable distances.
accordionPanel3Content: The Kids in Parks program uses guided activities and challenges to promote outdoor learning and exploration.
amenities: Adventure; Hiking; Biking; Water Sports; Fishing

name: Brew Ridge Trail
description: Embark on an unforgettable journey along the Brew Ridge Trail, a self-guided adventure that showcases six of the nation's finest craft breweries. Nestled in the picturesque landscape of Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains, this trail offers a delightful variety of brews, from refreshing lagers to rich stouts, ensuring there's something for every palate. As you traverse the scenic route, you'll also encounter charming stops like Inglewood Farm and Montebello Fish Hatchery, as well as the renowned Veritas Vineyards & Winery. Enjoy breathtaking views, indulge in tastings, and discover the artistry behind each craft beer. Whether you're a seasoned connoisseur or a curious newcomer, the Brew Ridge Trail promises a memorable exploration of local flavors and stunning surroundings.
image1Desc: Circular logo with beer glasses, text: 'Brew Ridge Trail, Virginia's Original Beer Trail.'
address: Route 151 Craft Beverage Corridor, Nelson County, VA 22958
amenities: Beer; Hiking; Tastings; Scenic Views; Biking

name: Nelson 151
description: Nestled in the scenic northern part of Nelson County, Nelson 151 is a delightful escape for outdoor enthusiasts and wine lovers alike. Here, visitors can explore five charming wineries, including the renowned Veritas Vineyards & Winery and Mountain and Vine Winery, each offering tastings with breathtaking views of the Blue Ridge Mountains. For those seeking a refreshing brew, three local breweries, such as Blue Mountain Brewery, and a delightful cidery provide ample options. After a day of exploration, unwind at one of the cozy Bed & Breakfasts or connect with friendly farmers at local markets. With its stunning landscapes and vibrant local culture, Nelson 151 promises a memorable experience for all who venture here.
image1Desc: Mountain silhouette with text 'NELSON 151' on dark blue shield.
amenities: Beer; Cider; Spirits; Hiking; Scenic Views; Biking; Farm; Tastings; Fishing

name: Nelson 29
description: Embark on a delightful journey along the Nelson 29 craft beverage route, a scenic pathway that connects 29 unique breweries, wineries, and distilleries between Arrington and Faber. This charming route invites you to savor local flavors, from the exquisite wines at Veritas Vineyards & Winery to the refreshing brews at Blue Mountain Brewery. Explore the picturesque landscapes surrounding Inglewood Farm and Deer Creek Farm, and don't miss the serene views at the Montebello Fish Hatchery. With each stop, you'll discover the rich heritage and craftsmanship behind Virginia's finest beverages, making it a perfect outing for enthusiasts and casual visitors alike. Whether you're tasting artisanal spirits or enjoying a picnic at one of the scenic venues, Nelson 29 promises a memorable experience filled with natural beauty and local culture.
image1Desc: Green shield with 'Nelson 29 Craft Beverage Trail' text and mountain silhouette.

name: Nelson Scoops

amenities: Desserts; Family Friendly

name: Virginia Spirits Trail
description: Discover the Virginia Spirits Trail, a captivating journey through the heart of Virginia’s artisanal distilling scene. This trail celebrates the pride and craftsmanship behind each small-batch spirit, emphasizing the farm-to-bottle ethos that enriches every sip. As you explore, visit charming locales like Inglewood Farm and Deer Creek Farm, where local ingredients shine. Don’t miss the chance to unwind at scenic spots like Veritas Vineyards & Winery and Blue Mountain Brewery, where you can savor delightful pairings of spirits and local brews. Experience the soul of Virginia in every bottle, and immerse yourself in the rich flavors and traditions that define this unique trail.

Enjoy breathtaking rolling pasture views as you wake up to the sounds of nature. Spend your days exploring the farm's private hiking loops, where scenic trails lead you through picturesque landscapes. In the evening, unwind on the dedicated stargazing deck, sipping a vintage from nearby wineries or a refreshing brew from Blue Mountain Brewery. With modern amenities, including a full kitchenette, Crestvue Cottage is the perfect retreat for those seeking relaxation and adventure in a beautiful setting.
